title: Split compound heat/sample keys
scenario: Hervani Testworks has 52 invented key strings HEAT|SAMPLE|ORIENTATION. Mixed orientation case and ordinary spaces are present; two malformed records lack delimiters. Return Missing for a malformed key rather than guessing its components.

lesson.intro: Delimiter-based extraction works when segment lengths vary. Identify whether you need the first delimiter, last delimiter or a nested extraction. Validate the stated malformed case.

functions.name: TEXTBEFORE
functions.arguments: Provide input and delimiter; optional instance chooses occurrence, match_mode controls case, match_end treats end as delimiter, and if_not_found supplies a fallback.
functions.useCase: Extract the heat portion of a compound ID.
functions.mistake: Negative instance numbers search from the end. Missing delimiters need an explicit fallback.

functions.name: TEXTAFTER
functions.arguments: Arguments mirror TEXTBEFORE: input, delimiter, occurrence, case mode, end matching, and missing fallback.
functions.useCase: Extract a sample or order segment.
functions.mistake: The first and last delimiter produce different results in multi-part keys.

lesson.combine: Reuse IFERROR for Missing and TRIM/UPPER to normalize extracted text. Extraction alone is not validation: a delimiter-free string needs an explicit fallback.

tasks.prompt: For the first six records, return the heat segment before the first |, trimmed; return Missing when no delimiter exists.
For the first six records, return the orientation after the last |, trimmed and uppercase; preserve the mixed-case fallback Missing.
For the first six records, return the sample segment between the two delimiters; return Missing for malformed keys.
For the first six records, return Transverse when the normalized final orientation is TWA, Longitudinal for LPA, or Missing for a malformed key.

bonus.prompt: Return the first row’s heat segment plus / plus sample segment.
